# Instructions for agents

Read this file, then [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md), before changing anything. Your role's prompt is in
[`.bive/prompts/`](.bive/prompts/).

## Roles

- **Owner**: the human owner alone holds supervisory authority: authorizes work and merges, merges or closes pull
  requests, approves teams and the three gates, arbitrates shared files, and releases tests. The owner merges with
  GitHub's merge commit, pinned to the checked head, after the owner-applied dated label turns
  `bive-merge-gate / merge-gate` green. Whoever merges did not write. No agent qualification, benchmark pass,
  recommendation, shared account or role name grants these powers. No agent approves or merges into `main`.
- **Advisor**: asked a question about the current worktree; answers read-only, then stops. Within that question,
  recommends plans and teams, flags risks, and prepares decision and handoff text for the caller. Advice is not
  authorization. Never authorizes work or merges, closes pull requests, approves teams or gates, releases tests, or
  acts as coordinator or delegate. Historical supervisor qualifications grant no authority.
- **Coordinator**: one per milestone branch (`milestone/<name>`; Bive's own is `bived`), at most two at once, each
  started with the owner's approval in its own clone; it approves only pull requests based on its branch. Splits, briefs,
  starts delegates, creates and reviews issue pull requests, approves them and asks the owner to merge. Never
  merges, never closes a pull request, never pushes to the integration branch or `main`, never writes product code: a
  delegate's work that failed twice is split again or raised at gate 2, not taken over (owner, 2026-11-09). Its own
  pull requests (the inviolable files, `HANDOFF.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) go the same way: a branch, a pull request labelled
  `coordinator`, the owner's merge.
- **Delegate**: one issue and one worktree; pushes its branch, returns its report to the coordinator, then stops.
  Never creates a pull request or starts another agent.

## Rules

- **One branch and one pull request per issue**: `issue/<n>-<slug>`. Only the coordinator creates pull requests for
  issue work, after receiving the pushed branch and delegate's report. The body starts with `Closes #N` (or `Part of
  #N` and what is left) and holds the delegate's report.
- **Claim the issue** with a short comment before working on it; update it with the result.
- **Stay in your worktree**: the guard plugin refuses writes outside it, including shell redirections; a delegate's
  commands may not name any path outside it (absolute, `~`, `$HOME`, `..`) apart from the system folders. A
  delegate's worktree is `.worktrees/issue-<n>`, inside the checkout and git-ignored (never `../<repo>-<n>`: the
  coordinator's session may not write there).
- **Never**: force-push, rewrite pushed history, push to `main`, `rm -rf`, kill processes by pattern (`pkill -f`,
  `killall`); record the PID of each process you start and target that PID when stopping it. Never read SSH keys or the
  private paths listed in `opencode.jsonc`.
- **Keep sessions and prompts short**: continue a stuck delegate with one short message rather than a new session;
  a brief names files to read instead of pasting them. Delegate in small tasks with their own done-when and tests.
- **Keep `HANDOFF.md` and `ROADMAP.md` true**: the coordinator updates them once per batch of merges, in the same
  commit as the code they describe. Delete what is no longer accurate rather than adding contradictions.

## Coding rules

Generic, whatever the language (owner, 2026-11-08, taken from the practice of the owner's first project). The project's own rules go under
*Project rules* below.

- **Everything in English**: interface, code, comments, docstrings, documentation.
- **Fail-safe**: no exception swallowed in silence (catch the precise one, or log once and say why); a timeout on
  every subprocess and every network call; a file the program reads may be missing or corrupt without a crash.
- **A linter in the fast checks**; never reformat a whole file; every suppressed warning says why, in parentheses.
- **Tests in three tiers**: *fast* (the delegate, before handing its branch and report to the coordinator: lint and
  the tests of the files touched),
  *core* (the coordinator, once per batch of merges, never after each merge), *full* (before a release).
  CI is separate: run automated checks on pull requests and pushes to the default and integration branches, so a red
  base is visible quickly; this does not replace the coordinator's once-per-batch local core run.
- **Docs change in the same commit** as the code they describe (README, reference pages, HANDOFF, ROADMAP).
- **Commits are authored by the agent that made them, under an explicit name** (owner, 2026-11-08): in its working
  copy an agent sets `git config --worktree user.name "<role> <provider/model>"`, the model's name **and version**,
  the same name as in the registry's llm variable (e.g. `delegate anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, never `delegate` or
  `Claude`), and `git config --worktree user.email "<role>@bive.invalid"`, never the owner's identity. `--worktree`
  is required: plain `git config` writes the config every worktree shares, so one delegate's name becomes everyone's;
  it needs `git config extensions.worktreeConfig true` once per clone. The name is that of the model running now:
  when the session's model changes, set it again before the next commit and sign comments with the new name. Merges
  are merge commits made by the owner, so every commit keeps its author; GitHub's squash button would attribute
  the result to the account that pressed it and is disabled in the repository's settings. Anyone must be able to tell
  from `git log` who wrote each change, human or model.
- **No Git hooks**: a delegate is started by the coordinator, never by a Git command.

## Inviolable prompts

- **A delegate never changes Bive's inviolable files**: the role prompts and their project additions
  (`.bive/prompts/`), the templates (`.bive/templates/`), the plugins (`.opencode/plugins/`), `opencode.jsonc`,
  `.bive/registry-id`, this file and the `bive-*` workflows. If one is wrong, it says so in its report. The guard
  plugin refuses these writes (each refusal counts as a violation in the registry) and the `bive-inviolable` check
  fails any `issue/*` pull request that touches them, unless it carries the label `coordinator`: the coordinator's
  own pull requests, the only ones that may change these files (only the coordinator sets that label).
- **Others complete, never edit, the role prompts**: the owner or the coordinator adds to a role in
  `.bive/prompts/project/<ROLE>.md`, which may narrow a rule but never loosen or contradict one; the core prompt wins.

## Field reports

- **When**: at the end of each milestone (with gate 3), and at once when a Bive rule, prompt, template or plugin had
  to be worked around or overridden.
- **How**: the coordinator  fills `.bive/templates/field-report.md`: numbered remarks, each with
  what happened (numbers), what worked, the proposed change and the Bive file it touches. The project's owner passes
  it to Bive's owner, who files one issue per change in Bive's repository.
- **No names**: no project, product, repository, person, host, path or private data; "a project", "machine A",
  "the owner". Model ids stay canonical (Bive needs them per model).

## What goes into Bive

Nothing enters the template that is not read by one of the three roles, or by a human, during a task (owner,
2026-11-08). Anything else (a public page, a visualisation, a helper for the registry) lives in its own repository.

- **GitHub PR merge methods (owner, 2026-11-09)**: `merge` only. The desired repository setting, not an automatic

- core (coordinator, once per batch): `node --test tests/*.test.ts`; `opencode plugin list` shows every Bive plugin with a
  real ID (not `-`), run after a session has started in the checkout (before that it lists none).

# Milestone workspace

A minimal, reusable Bive workspace for the human owner, coordinators, delegates, and read-only advisors. It contains role instructions, report templates, and required-check workflows, but no project history or user data.

Read `AGENTS.md` and `HANDOFF.md` first, then the prompt of the role the owner assigns. There is no default OpenCode
agent (the workspace once defaulted to the `supervisor` agent): the owner selects the agent and the model for each
assignment. `.bive/prompts/SUPERVISOR.md` is a retired compatibility pointer; it grants no authority.

## Checks

Run `node --check .github/scripts/check-merge-gate.mjs`, `node --check .github/scripts/merge-gate-lib.mjs`, and `node --test tests/*.test.ts` with Node 22 or newer.

## Repository settings

Use merge commits only. On each active milestone branch require pull requests, `tests`, and `merge-gate`, including for administrators; prohibit deletion and force pushes. On `main` require pull requests and `tests`. Protect the branches after initial setup, and verify the settings through GitHub's API. A green check alone is not branch protection.

Creating a repository from this template copies files, not issues, pull requests, labels, or branch protection. Configure each repository independently.

# Project additions to the role prompts

Bive's role prompts (`../SUPERVISOR.md`, `../COORDINATOR.md`, `../DELEGATE.md`) are inviolable: nobody edits them in a
project. To add to a role, the supervisor or the coordinator writes `<ROLE>.md` here (e.g. `DELEGATE.md`); an agent
reads it right after its role prompt. An addition may narrow or detail a rule, never loosen or contradict one: where
they differ, the core prompt wins. Delegates never change this folder either.

# Handoff

## Goal

Resolve the assigned milestone using the role boundaries in `AGENTS.md`.

## Running it

- Node 22 or newer; Git and GitHub CLI authenticated for this repository.
- There is no default agent: the owner selects the OpenCode agent and model for each assignment. (The workspace
  previously started a `supervisor` agent with `.bive/prompts/SUPERVISOR.md` as its system prompt; that prompt is now
  a retired compatibility pointer with no authority.)
- Read `ROADMAP.md` and the repository's issues and pull requests for the current assignment.
- No registry participation, external services, private data, or background workers are configured.

## Decisions

- **Owner-approved coordinator teams (owner, 2026-11-13)**: prefer the strongest suitable verified-free usable
  coordinator; otherwise recommend a suitable usable coordinator from the current supervisor provider. Before launch
  or substitution, ask the owner to approve the concrete team, cost, availability evidence, alternatives, and fallback,
  then stop and wait. No silent coordinator substitution or inference that unknown pricing is free. Existing
  qualifications, allow-lists, delegate fallback, and role rights remain unchanged. See `docs/PROVIDERS.md` and the
  supervisor's project additions.
- The owner alone merges or closes pull requests, using merge commits. Coordinators review, open pull requests and
  hand over; delegates implement their assigned issues and never open a pull request.
- **Owner authority (owner, 2026-11-14)**: the human owner alone authorizes work and merges, merges or closes pull
  requests, approves teams and gates, arbitrates shared files, and releases tests; no agent approves or merges into
  `main`. A qualification or a green check never grants authority.
- **Read-only advisor (owner, 2026-11-14)**: an advisor answers one question about the current worktree, read-only,
  then stops: no writes, comments, reviews, commands, or launches. Advice is never authorization, and an advisor is
  not a standing manager or a rung of authority.
- **Hand-over launch (owner, 2026-11-14)**: advice-prepared launch text is a proposal until the owner records approval
  of the scope and the team.

## Tasks

Await the owner's milestone assignment.

# Roadmap

Resolve the milestone assigned by the owner. Issues define the done-when criteria; pull-request reports and green checks do not substitute for completion evidence.

- Gate 1: the owner agrees the split; every issue has a done-when and checks, with shared files arbitrated.
- Gate 2: a delegate that failed twice is split again or raised to the owner; a coordinator does not take over implementation.
- Gate 3: review the milestone's completion, outstanding issues, and required checks before merging to main.

# The coordinator's routine, as commands

What `.bive/prompts/COORDINATOR.md` steps 5, 7 and 9 mean at the shell, for a coordinator that wants the exact
commands. `<n>` is the issue, `<slug>` a short name, `<base>` the integration branch, `<model>` the delegate's
`provider/model`.

## Session start

The label the owner applies to authorize a merge must exist that day (owner, 2026-11-10). Create it, never rename an
older one: renaming moves the label onto every pull request that carries it and would re-date the owner's past
authorizations. The coordinator never applies it.

```bash
label="bive-merge-authorized-until-$(date -u +%F)"
gh label list --search "$label" --json name --jq '.[].name' | grep -qx "$label" \
  || gh label create "$label" --color B60205 --description "Owner only: authorizes one merge through $(date -u +%F) UTC"
```

## Start a delegate (step 5)

```bash
git worktree add .worktrees/issue-<n> -b issue/<n>-<slug> <base>
git config extensions.worktreeConfig true                     # once per clone
git -C .worktrees/issue-<n> config --worktree user.name "delegate <model>"
git -C .worktrees/issue-<n> config --worktree user.email delegate@bive.invalid
mkdir -p .worktrees/issue-<n>/.bive/state
echo delegate > .worktrees/issue-<n>/.bive/state/role          # the guard's sign
# the brief: .bive/templates/brief.md filled into .bive/state/briefs/<n>.md
gh issue comment <n> --body "Started: branch issue/<n>-<slug>, delegate <model>"
brief="$(cat .bive/state/briefs/<n>.md)"                        # read here: outside the delegate's worktree
(cd .worktrees/issue-<n> && BIVE_ROLE=delegate opencode run --agent delegate --model <model> "$brief") &
echo $!                                                         # record the PID (AGENTS.md › Never)
```

The `delegate` agent of `opencode.jsonc` gives the session `.bive/prompts/DELEGATE.md` as its system prompt.
`opencode debug agents` lists the agents OpenCode resolved (OpenCode 2.2.5 has no `opencode agent` subcommand).

A project whose checks need a local environment links it into the worktree (for example
`ln -s "$PWD/.venv" .worktrees/issue-<n>/.venv`).

## Open and review a pull request (step 7)

The delegate pushes its branch and returns the filled report; it never opens a pull request. The coordinator creates
the PR from the pushed branch and uses the report as the PR body. For a multi-part issue, open/update it according to
the brief's timing. If the delegate's final response is not accessible from the coordinator's machine, recover the
report from the final pushed commit body (do not expect the delegate's ignored `.bive/state/` file to travel):

```bash
git fetch origin issue/<n>-<slug>
git show -s --format=%H FETCH_HEAD
git log -1 --format=%b FETCH_HEAD
```

The report's Log section should name the commit SHA; the coordinator fills it in if the report was carried in that
commit body. Save the report on the coordinator's machine in `.bive/state/briefs/<n>-report.md`, then run:

```bash
gh pr create --base <base> --head issue/<n>-<slug> --title "#<n>: <title>" --body-file .bive/state/briefs/<n>-report.md
```

The report body starts with `Closes #<n>` when complete, or `Part of #<n>` and what remains.

```bash
gh pr view <pr> --json body,baseRefName,files,commits \
  --jq '.body, .baseRefName, (.files[].path), (.commits[].authors[] | "\(.name) <\(.email)>")'
```

Read it against the checklist: first line `Closes #N` / `Part of #N`; the sections State, Changed, Checks, Left, Log
filled and no `<!--` left; the base; no path matching the inviolable list (`AGENTS.md` › Inviolable prompts, the same
list as `bive-inviolable`); every author `delegate <provider/model> <delegate@bive.invalid>`. Then the brief's checks
in the worktree if the head changed since the report, and the diff. Then wait for CI and hand over:

```bash
gh pr checks <pr> --watch                      # returns when the checks finish; every one but bive-merge-gate green
gh pr review <pr> --approve --body "Ready to merge: <the checks you ran>"
```

The owner merges (`gh pr merge <pr> --merge --match-head-commit <sha>`, after the owner-applied label); pull requests
waiting for the owner: `gh pr list --base <base> --search "review:approved"`. The coordinator never merges, closes or
pushes to `<base>`. To be told when a pull request is merged without a watcher plugin: `gh pr checks` for the checks, then
`until [ "$(gh pr view <pr> --json state --jq .state)" != OPEN ]; do sleep 60; done` in the shell, when a session
really needs to wait; most of the time the next session reads `gh pr list` instead.
Once merged, if the issue is still open (GitHub closes on the default branch only):

```bash
gh issue close <n> --comment "Done in <base> (PR #<pr>)"
```

`bive-merge-gate / merge-gate` stays red on every pull request until the owner applies the dated label
`bive-merge-authorized-until-YYYY-MM-DD` (`docs/REQUIRED-CHECKS.md`): read that red as "waiting for the owner's label",
not as a failure to brief again. The coordinator never applies the label.

## After the batch (step 9)

The core checks once, after the last merge, then `HANDOFF.md` and `ROADMAP.md` in one commit on a coordinator branch,
opened as a pull request labelled `coordinator` and merged by the owner like any other. Clean up:
`git worktree list`, then `git worktree remove .worktrees/issue-<n>` for each merged issue (never forced).

## Two coordinators at once

The owner starts one coordinator per milestone branch, at most two at once (`AGENTS.md` › Roles). Each works in its own
clone, because `.worktrees/`, `.bive/state/` and the guard belong to one checkout:

```bash
git clone <repository> <dir> && cd <dir> && git switch milestone/<name>
gh pr list --base milestone/<name>                    # the pull requests this coordinator reviews, and no others
gh pr list --label coordinator --state open           # before opening a coordinator PR on an inviolable file: empty
```

At gate 1 each milestone lists the files it will touch; where the two lists overlap, the owner names one writer
or the order, and the brief says so. Each coordinator writes only its milestone's section of `HANDOFF.md` and
`ROADMAP.md`.

## GitHub pull-request merge methods

The repository allows `merge` only (`AGENTS.md` › Project rules): a merge commit keeps every delegate's commit under
its author; squash would attribute the result to the account that pressed the button. The owner keeps **Settings →
General → Pull Requests** aligned.

## Scripting it

A project may script this routine in its own repository (start, review, status, clean): one Python / ImGui project
did, in about 400 lines with tests, and used it for a whole batch. Bive ships no such script (HANDOFF › Decisions,
*No machinery*): the prompt and this page are enough for any coordinator, and a script stays the project's own,
outside Bive's files.

# Provider fallback

No automatic provider probe by default. Each role lists models in order in `.bive/models.json`; when a delegate call
fails (unreachable, 429, quota), the coordinator retries the same brief with the next delegate model and says so in the
report. Coordinator launch and substitution require the owner-approved team described below, not automatic fallback.
When every model of the list failed, a project can offer a provider search: a script (or MCP tool) that tries every
model OpenCode knows with one tiny prompt and prints the ones that answer, fastest first, as a `.bive/models.json`
line. A delegate's work that a reviewer rejects is redone by the next model, not patched by the same one.

## Coordinator selection and owner-approved team

Before starting or replacing a coordinator, the owner-approved team rules below apply; the owner alone approves the
team and records that approval. The legacy supervisor project additions (`.bive/prompts/project/SUPERVISOR.md`) are
retired and grant no authority. Prefer the strongest suitable model whose current free pricing and usability can be
verified, while preserving every existing qualification and owner allow-list requirement. A listing is not
availability, a successful tiny request is not a capability benchmark, and unknown pricing is not free. State the
evidence and uncertainty instead of claiming an objectively best model without a comparison.

Inspect the available catalog and existing results first. Manually check a shortlisted model with one small synthetic
request, no tools or private context, and a timeout; record the canonical/resolved ID, UTC time, pricing source, and
outcome. Do not sweep providers or incur paid/unknown-cost checks without owner permission. Availability is temporary:
recheck before launch if the evidence is stale or the account, machine, or quota changed.

If no suitable verified-free coordinator is usable, recommend the strongest suitable usable model from the provider of the session preparing the proposal, unless the
owner names another provider. Do not silently substitute a paid model,
cross providers, buy credits, or turn on billing. A named but unfunded model is not a usable launch choice.

Ask the owner to approve a concrete team before launching or switching a coordinator:

| Item | What the proposal states |
| --- | --- |
| Needed roles | Coordinator, delegate, and advisor (read-only advice) only where the task needs them; canonical model/version per role |
| Suitability | Relevant results, task fit, qualification or allow-list status, and limitations |
| Cost and availability | Verified-free, paid, or unknown; evidence source and recent check time/outcome |
| Recommendation | Best supported team, alternatives, current-provider fallback, and a wait/stop choice |
| Approval | Exact requested launch or change and any cost; stop and wait for the owner's answer |

No general milestone mandate authorizes a model change. On credit, service, rate-limit, or quota failure, preserve the
session and work, explain the infrastructure blocker, and obtain approval of the revised team before another
coordinator takes over. Record the approved model and reason in the handoff and set its Git identity before its next
commit. An outage alone is not evidence of poor model judgement; assess separately how an agent handles it. This
policy changes neither delegate fallback nor role rights, merge gates, or qualifications. Advice-prepared launch text
is a proposal until the owner records approval of the scope and the team; a qualification or a green check never
grants authority.

## Per-machine model aliases

`.bive/models.json` is shared and contains canonical model IDs. If a machine serves one of those models through a
different OpenCode provider ID, keep a local, untracked mapping in `.bive/state/models.local.json`:

```json
{
  "aliases": {
    "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5": "claude-agent/sonnet"
  }
}
```

The keys are canonical IDs from `.bive/models.json`; values are the `provider/model` IDs that work on this machine.
`.bive/state/` is git-ignored, so never commit this file; it contains model IDs only, not credentials. If it is absent
or unreadable, use the canonical ID and tell the owner. Keep the canonical model in the worktree-specific Git author
identity (`git config --worktree user.name`) as required by `AGENTS.md`; when useful, report both the canonical and
resolved IDs.

OpenCode configuration can add or override model IDs under a provider, and `modelID` can change the ID sent to that
provider. That is useful when only the upstream model ID differs. It does not directly alias a canonical
`provider/model` reference to a different OpenCode provider/model pair, so use the local map when provider IDs differ.

Before dispatching a model on a new machine, check that the resolved ID answers:

```bash
opencode run -m <provider/model> "Reply with your model id only."
```

This is a one-model manual check, not an automatic provider search. For a delegate, an unavailable model or an
insufficient-funds error counts as a model error; continue to the next canonical delegate model in `.bive/models.json`,
applying its local alias if present. For a coordinator, stop and seek owner approval of the revised team instead.

# Required checks

Bive's expected checks before merging a pull request. This page is a repository-readable inventory: it names the
automated GitHub Actions checks, their conditions, and the checks that are run locally by a coordinator. It describes
Bive's intended merge policy and maps to the workflow files; it does **not** prove which checks GitHub branch
protection currently requires (that configuration lives in the repository's settings). The workflow files named below
are the source to compare against and to update when check names or behavior change.

## Automated checks (GitHub Actions)

These run on GitHub and appear as commit statuses on a pull request.

### `bive-tests / tests`

- **Workflow file**: `.github/workflows/bive-tests.yml`
- **Job**: `tests`
- **Triggers**: `push` to `main` and `bived`; `pull_request` (default activity types: `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`).
- **Runs**: `ubuntu-latest`, Node 22, `node --test tests/*.test.ts`, timeout 10 minutes.
- **What it checks**: the repository's test suite (`tests/*.test.ts`).
- **Expected on PRs**: yes — the `pull_request` trigger runs it on pull requests (default activity types).

### `bive-inviolable / check`

- **Workflow file**: `.github/workflows/bive-inviolable.yml`
- **Job**: `check`
- **Triggers**: `pull_request` of types `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`, `labeled`, `unlabeled`.
- **Condition (job `if`)**: runs only when `github.head_ref` starts with `issue/` **and** the pull request does not
  carry the `coordinator` label:
  `startsWith(github.head_ref, 'issue/') && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'coordinator')`.
- **What it checks**: compares the changed files against the base branch and fails if any inviolable path changed.
  The matched paths are: `.bive/registry-id`, anything under `.bive/prompts/` or `.bive/templates/`, anything under
  `.opencode/plugins/` or `.opencode/plugin/`, files matching `.github/workflows/bive-*`, `opencode.jsonc`, and
  `AGENTS.md`.
- **Skip conditions** (the job is skipped, not failed):
  - the head branch does not start with `issue/` (for example a coordinator's own pull request on another branch);
  - the pull request carries the `coordinator` label (a coordinator's own pull request that legitimately changes an
    inviolable file).
- **Why**: a delegate's pull request must never change Bive's inviolable files (see `AGENTS.md` › Inviolable prompts).
  Only the coordinator changes them, and only on pull requests it labels `coordinator`.

### `bive-merge-gate / merge-gate`

- **Workflow file**: `.github/workflows/bive-merge-gate.yml`; script `.github/scripts/check-merge-gate.mjs`, decision
  in `.github/scripts/merge-gate-lib.mjs`.
- **Job**: `merge-gate`
- **Triggers**: `pull_request_target` on pull requests targeting `bived` or `milestone/**`, types `opened`,
  `synchronize`, `reopened`, `labeled`, `unlabeled`. It checks out the base commit only and never runs code from the
  pull request's head; its permissions are read-only (`contents`, `pull-requests`, `checks`).
- **Runs**: `ubuntu-latest`, Node 22, timeout 15 minutes. It waits (every 10 seconds, at most 12 minutes, each `gh`
  call limited to 15 seconds) until the other checks have finished, then decides.
- **Authorization**: exactly one label `bive-merge-authorized-until-YYYY-MM-DD` on the pull request, a real calendar
  date, valid through 23:59:59 UTC of that date and only while the base is `bived` or `milestone/<name>` (one path
  segment). Only the owner applies it, after the coordinator's approval and when the owner is about to merge;
  the coordinator never does, also on its own pull requests. Adding or removing it re-runs the gate.
- **Red before the label is expected**: on every pull request without the label the gate fails with "exactly one
  dated merge-authorization label is required". It means "waiting for the owner", not a failure to fix.
- **What it checks**: the authorization above; exactly one `bive-tests / tests` and one `bive-inviolable / check`,
  both `pass`; every other check except its own `pass` as well. The one accepted exception: `bive-inviolable / check`
  may be `skipping` on a pull request labelled `coordinator` (its job condition skips it there). It re-reads the pull
  request after reading the checks and fails if the head, base or labels changed.
- **Fails on**: a missing, malformed, duplicate or expired label; any check pending past the deadline, missing,
  skipped (other than the exception), failed or cancelled; a pull request whose head or base changed during the run.
- **Several coordinators**: each approves only pull requests based on its own milestone branch; the gate does not
  check which coordinator approved, each coordinator enforces that itself (`AGENTS.md` › Roles).
- **Expiry is not re-evaluated on its own**: a gate that passed stays green after its date. The owner applies the
  label dated the day of the merge, and the owner merges that day with `gh pr merge --merge
  --match-head-commit <sha>`, so a push after the gate's run refuses the merge.

## Branch protection (owner, in GitHub's settings)

The workflows report checks; they do not make GitHub enforce them. For the gate to block GitHub's merge button and
direct pushes, the owner configures branch protection (or a ruleset) on `bived` and `milestone/*` to
require the status checks `bive-merge-gate / merge-gate` and `bive-tests / tests`; the gate itself judges
`bive-inviolable / check`, including its skip on coordinator pull requests. A ruleset names a required check by its
job (check-run) name alone, `merge-gate` and `tests` with GitHub Actions as source: every workflow's job keeps a
name of its own, or the requirement matches several checks (#94). Until that configuration exists, the
gate is only as strong as the owner's merge procedure. No file in this repository proves that it exists; check the
settings.

## Local and manual checks (not GitHub statuses)

These are run by people or agents on their own machine. They are **not** GitHub required statuses and do not appear as
commit checks on a pull request.

- **Fast checks (delegate)**: lint and the tests of the files touched, for example
  `node --test tests/<the test of the file touched>.test.ts`.
- **Core checks (coordinator, once per batch of merges)**: `node --test tests/*.test.ts`; and
  `opencode plugin list` showing every Bive plugin with a real ID (not `-`), run after a session has started in the
  checkout.
- **Full checks (before a release)**: the two above, plus a fresh-clone install check where a write to
  `../outside.txt` is refused by the guard and `.bive/state/tokens.jsonl` fills.
- **`opencode plugin list`** is a local/manual check; it is not a GitHub required status.

## What this document does not say

- It does not prove which checks GitHub branch protection currently requires, nor that any check is marked
  "required" in repository settings. Branch protection and rulesets are configured under the repository's settings;
  compare them against the checks listed here.
- It does not say who merges: the owner alone, after the coordinator's review (`AGENTS.md` › Roles).
- Workflow job names are part of the check identity. If a workflow or job is renamed, update this document and the
  repository's branch-protection configuration together so they keep matching.
